source.text: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναστὰς ἔρχεται εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ὡς εἰώθει πάλιν ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And from there having risen up he comes into the regions of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and come together again crowds to him, and as he was accustomed again he was teaching them.

en.L: And rising up from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes into the regions of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and crowds again come together to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was accustomed, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was again teaching them.
en.B: Jesus set out from there and came to the districts of Judea and the land beyond the Jordan. Crowds came together around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them once more, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} usually did.
en.R: Jesus left Capernaum and went south to the land of Judea and to the area on the east side of the Jordan River. Again crowds of people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And Jesus taught them, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} always did.

vi.L: Và từ đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đứng dậy, đi đến miền Giu-đê và bên kia [sông] Giô-đanh, và các đoàn dân đông lại tụ họp đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và như thường lệ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại dạy dỗ họ.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu rời nơi đó và đến miền Giu-đê và vùng bên kia sông Giô-đanh. Dân chúng lại kéo đến quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại dạy dỗ họ như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn thường làm.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu rời Ca-bê-na-um và đi về phía nam, đến miền Giu-đê và vùng phía đông sông Giô-đanh. Dân chúng lại kéo đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rất đông. Và Đức Giê-xu dạy dỗ họ như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn luôn làm.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 거기에서 일어나 유대 지역과 요단 강 건너편으로 가신다. 그러자 무리가 다시 그분께로 모여든다. 그리고 그분은 늘 하시던 대로 다시 그들을 가르치셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그곳을 떠나 유대 지방과 요단 강 건너편으로 가셨다. 무리가 다시 예수께로 모여들자, 예수께서는 늘 하시던 대로 다시 그들을 가르치셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 가버나움을 떠나 남쪽으로 가셨다. 그래서 유대 지방과 요단 강 동쪽 지역으로 가셨다. 거기에서도 많은 사람이 다시 예수께 모여들었다. 예수께서는 늘 하시던 대로 그들을 가르치셨다.

decisions.choice: comes, come together: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: he went, and the crowds gathered.

decisions.choice: the regions of Judea and beyond the Jordan: the land around Jerusalem and the land east of the river
decisions.reason: The land east of the Jordan was called Perea and was ruled by Herod Antipas. Jesus is now moving south toward Jerusalem (10:32).

decisions.choice: and beyond the Jordan
alternatives: through the region beyond the Jordan
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "through the region beyond the Jordan", which describes a route through Perea, and others leave out "and". The SBLGNT reads "and", naming two areas. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: from there: from Capernaum, where 9:33-50 took place
decisions.reason: The last place Mark names is the house in Capernaum (9:33).

decisions.choice: Capernaum; went south; the area on the east side of the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable names the place Jesus left and says where the land beyond the Jordan lay.

decisions.choice: historic present: "đi đến", "tụ họp" with no "đã" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense by leaving out the past marker; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past through the context. The same through Mark 10.

decisions.choice: "bên kia [sông] Giô-đanh"
decisions.reason: A Vietnamese reader needs to be told that the Jordan is a river.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), people speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("가신다", "말씀하신다"), through chapter 10
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (10:1, 10:11, 10:23-24, 10:27, 10:35, 10:42, 10:46, 10:49); Balanced and Readable use the past. Recorded once for the chapter.

decisions.choice: Protestant place names: "유대", "요단 강"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms (style guide, section 5), as in Mark 3:7-8.

source.text: Καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνδρὶ γυναῖκα ἀπολῦσαι, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were asking him if it is lawful for a husband a wife to divorce, testing him.

en.L: And they were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} if it is lawful for a husband to divorce a wife, testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Some people asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} whether the law allows a husband to divorce his wife. They were trying to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Some people came to test Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Does God's law let a man divorce his wife?"

vi.L: Và [người ta] hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có được phép cho người chồng bỏ vợ không, để thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Có mấy người hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xem luật pháp có cho phép người chồng ly dị vợ mình không. Họ muốn gài bẫy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Có mấy người đến để thử Đức Giê-xu. Họ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời có cho phép một người đàn ông ly dị vợ mình không?"

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그분을 시험하면서, 남편이 아내를 버리는 것이 옳은지 그분께 묻고 있었다.
ko.B: 어떤 사람들이 예수를 시험하려고, 남편이 아내와 이혼하는 것이 율법에 맞느냐고 예수께 물었다. 예수를 책잡으려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람들이 예수를 시험하려고 왔다. 그들이 예수께 물었다. "남자가 자기 아내와 이혼하는 것을 하나님의 율법이 허락합니까?"

decisions.choice: they were asking him: the SBLGNT does not name the questioners
alternatives: Pharisees came and were asking him
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read "Pharisees came up and asked him". A few early witnesses have only "they were asking him", and the SBLGNT follows them; the words about the Pharisees may have come in from Matthew 19:3. Either way, the question is put to test Jesus. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: testing: trying to trap him into a wrong or dangerous answer
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Satan in 1:13 and of the Pharisees in 8:11. Herod Antipas had put John to death for speaking against his marriage (6:17-18), and Jesus is now in Herod's territory.

decisions.choice: is it lawful: does the law of Moses allow it
alternatives: is it legal under Roman law
decisions.reason: Jews of the time agreed that the law allowed a husband to divorce. They argued over the grounds. Asking whether it was allowed at all invited Jesus to set himself against Moses.

decisions.choice: were asking: an imperfect, they kept pressing the question
decisions.reason: The tense can describe a question pressed or repeated.

decisions.choice: Some people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply a subject, since the SBLGNT does not name who asked.

decisions.choice: "bỏ vợ" (L); "ly dị" (B, R) for "divorce"
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is "release, send away"; Literal keeps that picture, Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word for divorce.

decisions.choice: "버리다" (L); "이혼하다" (B, R) for apolyo
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is "release, send away"; Literal keeps its picture with "버리다", which Korean also uses of a man leaving his wife, and Balanced and Readable say "divorce" plainly. The same pattern holds in 10:4, 10:11-12.

decisions.choice: "율법에 맞느냐" (B); "하나님의 율법이 허락합니까" (R)
decisions.reason: "Is it lawful" asks whether the law of Moses allows it (meaning decision); the archaic ending of the familiar versions is replaced by modern Korean.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί ὑμῖν ἐνετείλατο Μωϋσῆς;

records.literal_gloss: And he answering said to them, What you did command Moses?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "What did Moses command you?"
en.B: He replied with a question: "What did Moses command you?"
en.R: Jesus answered them with a question. He said, "What did Moses tell you to do?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời và nói với họ: "Môi-se đã truyền cho các người điều gì?"
vi.B: Ngài hỏi lại họ: "Môi-se đã truyền cho các người điều gì?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời bằng một câu hỏi: "Môi-se đã bảo các người phải làm gì?"

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 대답하여 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "모세가 너희에게 무엇이라고 명령하였느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 되물으셨다. "모세가 너희에게 무엇이라고 명령하였느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 질문으로 대답하셨다. "모세가 너희에게 어떻게 하라고 했느냐?"

decisions.choice: what did Moses command you: Jesus sends them back to the law
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with a question, as he does in 11:29-30. He uses the word "command"; in their reply they speak only of what Moses allowed (10:4).

decisions.choice: you: the questioners and Israel as a whole
decisions.reason: Moses gave the law to Israel, and Jesus speaks of it as given to them.

decisions.choice: "các người" for "you" (the questioners, 10:3-9)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to people who have come to test him, as he speaks to opponents in John.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἐπέτρεψεν Μωϋσῆς βιβλίον ἀποστασίου γράψαι καὶ ἀπολῦσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And they said, Permitted Moses a roll of divorce to write and to send away.

en.L: And they said, "Moses permitted [a man] to write a certificate of divorce and to send [her] away."
en.B: They said, "Moses allowed a man to write out a certificate of divorce and send his wife away."
en.R: They answered, "Moses let a man write his wife a paper saying they were divorced. Then he could send her away."

vi.L: Và họ nói: "Môi-se cho phép [người chồng] viết tờ ly dị và bỏ [vợ]."
vi.B: Họ đáp: "Môi-se cho phép người chồng viết giấy ly dị rồi cho vợ đi."
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Môi-se cho phép người chồng viết cho vợ một tờ giấy nói rằng họ đã ly dị. Rồi người chồng có thể cho vợ đi."

ko.L: 그들이 말했다. "모세는 이혼 증서를 써 주고 [아내를] 버리는 것을 허락했습니다."
ko.B: 그들이 대답했다. "모세는 남편이 이혼 증서를 써 주고 아내를 내보내는 것을 허락했습니다."
ko.R: 그들이 대답했다. "모세는 남자가 아내에게 이혼했다는 증서를 써 주고 아내를 내보내도 된다고 했습니다."

decisions.choice: a certificate of divorce: the rule in Deuteronomy 24:1-4
alternatives: a law of Moses not found in the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 24:1 speaks of a husband who writes his wife a certificate of divorce and sends her out of his house. The passage takes divorce for granted and limits what may follow it.

decisions.choice: certificate of divorce: a written document that set the woman free to marry again
decisions.reason: The husband himself wrote and gave the document. It gave the woman proof that she was no longer his wife.

decisions.choice: permitted: allowed, not commanded
decisions.reason: Jesus asked what Moses commanded (10:3); they answer with what Moses allowed.

decisions.choice: [a man] ... [her] (L); a man, his wife (B, R)
alternatives: to write and to send away
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the man and the woman to be understood. Literal brackets them; Balanced and Readable name them.

decisions.choice: "tờ ly dị" (L); "giấy ly dị" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The plain modern words for a written certificate of divorce.

decisions.choice: [아내를]
decisions.reason: Korean needs an object for "send away"; the subject can be left unsaid in Korean, so only the object is bracketed.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην·

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus said to them, Because of the hardness of heart of you he wrote for you the commandment this.

en.L: But Jesus said to them, "Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.
en.B: But Jesus told them, "It was because your hearts were hard that Moses wrote this commandment for you.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Moses wrote that rule for you because you were stubborn and would not obey God.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Vì lòng cứng cỏi của các người mà ông ấy đã viết điều răn này cho các người.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Chính vì lòng các người cứng cỏi mà Môi-se đã viết điều răn này cho các người.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Môi-se viết điều luật đó cho các người vì các người cứng lòng, không chịu vâng lời Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희 마음의 완고함 때문에 그가 너희에게 이 계명을 써 준 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희 마음이 굳어 있기 때문에 모세가 너희에게 이 계명을 써 준 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희가 고집이 세서 하나님께 순종하려 하지 않았기 때문에 모세가 그 규정을 써 준 것이다.

decisions.choice: hardness of heart: stubborn unwillingness to obey God
decisions.reason: The word is used in the Greek of Deuteronomy 10:16 and Jeremiah 4:4 for a heart that will not turn to God. Mark speaks of hard hearts in 3:5 and 6:52.

decisions.choice: the commandment was given because of sin, not as God's ideal
alternatives: divorce is wrong in every case under the law
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny that Moses wrote the rule. He says it was given to limit the harm done by people's hardness, while God's purpose is shown at creation (10:6-9).

decisions.choice: because of: on account of
decisions.reason: The preposition gives the reason the commandment was written.

decisions.choice: he wrote: Moses, named in 10:3-4
decisions.reason: The subject carries on from the previous verses.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses so that the subject is clear. Readable explains hardness of heart in plain words.

decisions.choice: "lòng cứng cỏi" (L, B); "cứng lòng" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has the same picture of a hard heart for stubbornness; Readable adds what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "마음의 완고함" (L); "마음이 굳어 있다" (B); "고집이 세서 하나님께 순종하려 하지 않다" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:5: Literal keeps the noun, Balanced keeps the picture in plain Korean, Readable says what it means (meaning decision). "완악" is the older church word.

source.text: ἀπὸ δὲ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: From however [the] beginning of creation male and female he made them.

en.L: But from [the] beginning of creation {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them male and female.
en.B: But at the beginning, when the world was created, God made them male and female.
en.R: But when God first created the world, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made people male and female.

vi.L: Nhưng từ ban đầu của sự sáng tạo, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã dựng nên họ là nam và nữ.
vi.B: Nhưng từ ban đầu, lúc sáng tạo thế giới, Đức Chúa Trời đã dựng nên con người có nam và có nữ.
vi.R: Nhưng khi Đức Chúa Trời mới tạo dựng thế giới, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã dựng nên con người có nam và có nữ.

ko.L: 그러나 창조의 처음부터 그들을 남자와 여자로 만드셨다.
ko.B: 그러나 처음 세상을 창조하실 때부터 하나님께서는 사람을 남자와 여자로 만드셨다.
ko.R: 그러나 하나님께서 처음 세상을 만드실 때, 사람을 남자와 여자로 만드셨다.

decisions.choice: male and female he made them: Genesis 1:27
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes Genesis 1:27 (and 5:2), which says God created humankind male and female.

decisions.choice: he made them: the SBLGNT does not name God
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "God" as the subject. The earliest leave it to be understood from the Genesis text. Either way God is the one who made them. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: from the beginning of creation: God's purpose from the start comes before the later rule
decisions.reason: Jesus sets what God did at creation above the permission given later in Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: God made (B); God first created ... he made (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, who is the subject in the Genesis text.

decisions.choice: no subject at Literal; the honorific "만드셨다" shows who made them
decisions.reason: The Greek does not name God (meaning decision); Korean can leave the subject unsaid, and the honorific verb is enough to show it is God. Balanced and Readable name him as the English does.

source.text: ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν· ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ μία σάρξ·

records.literal_gloss: On account of this will leave a man the father of him and the mother and will be joined to the wife of him, \v 8 and will be the two into flesh one; therefore no longer they are two but one flesh.

en.L: 'On account of this a man will leave his father and mother and will be joined to his wife, \v 8 and the two will become one flesh'; so they are no longer two, but one flesh.
en.B: 'This is why a man will leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife, \v 8 and the two of them will be one flesh.' And so they are two no longer, but one flesh.
en.R: God's word says, 'That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife. \v 8 The two of them will become one body.' So they are not two people anymore. They are one.

vi.L: 'Vì cớ đó, người nam sẽ lìa cha và mẹ mình mà gắn bó với vợ mình, \v 8 và hai người sẽ trở nên một thịt'; như vậy, họ không còn là hai nữa, nhưng là một thịt.
vi.B: 'Vì thế, người nam sẽ lìa cha mẹ mà gắn bó với vợ mình, \v 8 và hai người sẽ trở nên một thân.' Như vậy, họ không còn là hai nữa, nhưng là một thân.
vi.R: Lời Đức Chúa Trời chép: 'Vì thế, người đàn ông rời cha mẹ để gắn bó với vợ mình. \v 8 Hai người sẽ trở nên một thân.' Vậy họ không còn là hai người nữa. Họ là một.

ko.L: '이러므로 사람이 자기 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 자기 아내와 합하여, \v 8 그 둘이 한 몸이 될 것이다.' 그러므로 그들은 이제 둘이 아니라 한 몸이다.
ko.B: '그러므로 남자는 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 아내와 결합하고, \v 8 두 사람은 한 몸이 될 것이다.' 그러니 그들은 이제 둘이 아니라 한 몸이다.
ko.R: 성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있다. '그래서 남자는 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 아내와 하나가 된다. \v 8 두 사람은 한 몸이 된다.' 그러니 두 사람은 이제 둘이 아니라 하나이다.

decisions.choice: Genesis 2:24, quoted from the Greek version
decisions.reason: Jesus joins Genesis 2:24 to Genesis 1:27. The quotation follows the Greek translation of Genesis, which has "the two"; the Hebrew has "they".

decisions.choice: and will be joined to his wife: in the SBLGNT text
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack these words. The eye of a copyist could easily skip from one "and" to the next, or the words could have been added from Matthew 19:5 and Genesis. Without them, "the two" in 8a has no clear antecedent. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: become one flesh: become a single, united person and family
decisions.reason: In Hebrew thought flesh means a human being or a family tie (Genesis 29:14). The union includes the body but is more than that.

decisions.choice: so they are no longer two: Jesus draws the conclusion from the quotation
decisions.reason: The quotation ends with "one flesh". The next words are Jesus' own.

decisions.choice: a man: a male person, here a husband
decisions.reason: Genesis speaks of a man leaving his parents to be joined to his wife.

decisions.choice: God's word says
decisions.reason: Readable shows that Jesus is quoting Scripture. It says "one body" and "they are one" for one flesh.

decisions.choice: "một thịt" (L); "một thân" (B, R) for "one flesh"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word; "một thân" is the natural Vietnamese for one body, one person.

decisions.choice: "người nam" (L, B), "người đàn ông" (R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: A male person, a husband, is meant, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있다"
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jesus is quoting Scripture (Genesis 2:24), as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὃ οὖν ὁ θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.

records.literal_gloss: What therefore God has joined together, man not let separate.

en.L: So what God has joined together, let {{gender:no human|no man}} separate."
en.B: What God has yoked together, then, no human being is to separate."
en.R: God has joined the two of them together. So no one should separate them."

vi.L: Vậy điều gì Đức Chúa Trời đã kết hợp, thì loài người chớ phân rẽ."
vi.B: Vậy những gì Đức Chúa Trời đã kết hợp chung một ách, thì loài người không được phân rẽ."
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã kết hợp hai người lại với nhau. Vậy không ai được chia rẽ họ."

ko.L: 그러므로 하나님께서 한 멍에로 함께 매어 주신 것을 사람이 떼어 놓지 말아야 한다."
ko.B: 그러니 하나님께서 하나로 묶어 주신 것을 사람이 갈라놓아서는 안 된다."
ko.R: 하나님께서 두 사람을 하나로 맺어 주셨다. 그러니 아무도 그들을 갈라놓아서는 안 된다."

decisions.choice: joined together: yoked together, as two animals under one yoke
decisions.reason: The verb pictures two animals sharing one yoke and working as one. God himself makes the union.

decisions.choice: man: any human being, a husband or anyone else
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being. It sets human action against what God has done.

decisions.choice: what: neuter, the union itself
decisions.reason: The word points to the joined pair as one thing.

decisions.choice: yoked together
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the verb.

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L, B), "không ai" (R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words already mean any human being, so the English gender span has no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "kết hợp chung một ách" (yoked together)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the yoke that the Greek verb carries, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "한 멍에로 함께 매어 주다" (L); "하나로 묶어 주다" (B); "하나로 맺어 주다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to yoke together (meaning decision); Literal keeps the yoke, Balanced and Readable keep the sense of a binding union. "사람" for anthropos already means any human being, so no gender span is needed.

source.text: Καὶ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν πάλιν οἱ μαθηταὶ περὶ τούτου ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And in the house again the disciples concerning this were asking him.

en.L: And in the house the disciples were again asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about this.
en.B: Back in the house, the disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about this again.
en.R: Later, when they were inside the house, Jesus' followers asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said.

vi.L: Và vào trong nhà, các môn đồ lại hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về điều này.
vi.B: Khi về đến nhà, các môn đồ lại hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về điều ấy.
vi.R: Sau đó, khi đã vào trong nhà, các môn đồ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vừa nói.

ko.L: 그리고 집에서 제자들이 이것에 대하여 다시 그분께 묻고 있었다.
ko.B: 집에 돌아오자, 제자들이 이 일에 대해 다시 예수께 여쭈었다.
ko.R: 나중에 집 안에 들어갔을 때, 제자들이 예수께서 하신 말씀에 대해 여쭈어보았다.

decisions.choice: in the house again: again in private, as in 7:17 and 9:28
decisions.reason: "Again" may go with "in the house" (once more in private) or with the asking. Mark often has the disciples ask Jesus in private.

decisions.choice: about this: about what Jesus taught on divorce
decisions.reason: They ask about the teaching of 10:2-9.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable says "followers" for disciples, as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: "môn đồ" at Readable too
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese guide keeps "môn đồ" at every level, where the English Readable says "followers"; the same through Mark 10.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται ἐπ’ αὐτήν, καὶ ἐὰν αὐτὴ ἀπολύσασα τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς γαμήσῃ ἄλλον μοιχᾶται.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Whoever shall divorce the wife of him and marry another commits adultery against her; \v 12 and if she having divorced the husband of her should marry another, she commits adultery.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her; \v 12 and if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."
en.B: He told them, "A man commits adultery against his wife if he divorces her and marries another woman. \v 12 And a woman who divorces her husband and marries another man commits adultery."
en.R: Jesus said, "If a man divorces his wife and marries another woman, he is guilty of adultery against his first wife. \v 12 It is the same for a woman. If she divorces her husband and then marries another man, she is guilty of adultery."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Ai ly dị vợ mình và cưới người khác thì phạm tội ngoại tình đối với người vợ ấy; \v 12 và nếu chính người vợ ly dị chồng mình và lấy người khác, thì người ấy phạm tội ngoại tình."
vi.B: Ngài bảo họ: "Người nào ly dị vợ mình rồi cưới người phụ nữ khác là phạm tội ngoại tình đối với vợ mình. \v 12 Còn người vợ nào ly dị chồng rồi lấy người đàn ông khác cũng phạm tội ngoại tình."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Nếu một người đàn ông ly dị vợ mình rồi cưới người phụ nữ khác, thì người ấy phạm tội ngoại tình đối với người vợ đầu tiên. \v 12 Người phụ nữ cũng vậy. Nếu người ấy ly dị chồng rồi lấy người đàn ông khác, thì người ấy phạm tội ngoại tình."

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하신다. "누구든지 자기 아내를 버리고 다른 사람과 결혼하면, 그 아내에게 간음을 저지르는 것이다. \v 12 또 만일 아내가 자기 남편을 버리고 다른 사람과 결혼하면, 간음을 저지르는 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "누구든지 아내와 이혼하고 다른 여자와 결혼하면, 그 아내에게 간음하는 것이다. \v 12 또 아내가 남편과 이혼하고 다른 남자와 결혼하면, 간음하는 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "남자가 아내와 이혼하고 다른 여자와 결혼하면, 그 사람은 처음 아내에게 간음죄를 짓는 것이다. \v 12 여자도 마찬가지다. 여자가 남편과 이혼하고 다른 남자와 결혼하면, 그 여자도 간음죄를 짓는 것이다."

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: against her: against the first wife
decisions.reason: "Her" most likely refers to the wife he divorced: he wrongs her. It could refer to the new wife, with whom he commits adultery.

decisions.choice: if she divorces her husband: a wife's right under Greek and Roman law
alternatives: Jewish law gave women this right
decisions.reason: Under Jewish law only a husband could divorce. Greek and Roman law let a wife divorce her husband, and Herodias had left her first husband (6:17). Jesus' teaching applies to both.

decisions.choice: the man commits adultery against his wife: the husband is held to the same standard
alternatives: only a wife could be guilty of adultery
decisions.reason: In the custom of the time a man was thought to commit adultery only against another man's marriage. Jesus says a husband can wrong his own wife this way.

decisions.choice: if she divorces her husband and marries another
alternatives: if a woman leaves her husband and marries another
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts describe the woman as leaving or separating from her husband instead of divorcing him. The SBLGNT has the same verb as in 10:11. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: another woman; another man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant by "another". Readable also says whom the man wrongs, his first wife.

source.text: Καὶ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅψηται· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they were bringing to him little children that them he might touch; but the disciples rebuked them.

en.L: And they were bringing little children to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might touch them; but the disciples rebuked them.
en.B: People were bringing young children to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would touch them, but the disciples scolded them.
en.R: People brought their young children to Jesus. They wanted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to touch the children and bless them. But the followers told them off.

vi.L: Và [người ta] đem các trẻ nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chạm vào chúng; nhưng các môn đồ quở trách họ.
vi.B: Người ta đem các em nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chạm tay trên các em, nhưng các môn đồ rầy la họ.
vi.R: Người ta đem con nhỏ của mình đến với Đức Giê-xu. Họ muốn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chạm vào các em và chúc phước cho các em. Nhưng các môn đồ la rầy họ.

ko.L: 그리고 사람들이 그분께 어린아이들을 데려오고 있었다. 그분이 그들을 만져 주시게 하려는 것이었다. 그러나 제자들은 그들을 꾸짖었다.
ko.B: 사람들이 어린아이들을 예수께 데려왔다. 예수께서 아이들을 만져 주시기를 바랐던 것이다. 그런데 제자들이 그 사람들을 꾸짖었다.
ko.R: 사람들이 자기 어린아이들을 예수께 데려왔다. 예수께서 아이들에게 손을 얹고 복을 빌어 주시기를 바랐던 것이다. 그런데 제자들은 그 사람들을 나무랐다.

decisions.choice: touch: lay hands on them in blessing
decisions.reason: Parents asked respected teachers to bless their children by placing hands on them, as Jacob blessed Joseph's sons (Genesis 48:14). Jesus does this in 10:16.

decisions.choice: little children: young children, from infants to about twelve
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the twelve-year-old girl in 5:39-42.

decisions.choice: them: those who brought the children
decisions.reason: The disciples rebuke the people bringing the children, most likely their parents.

decisions.choice: were bringing: an imperfect, people kept coming
decisions.reason: The tense pictures a stream of people bringing children.

decisions.choice: and bless them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the touch was for, as 10:16 shows.

decisions.choice: "các trẻ nhỏ", "chúng" (L); "các em nhỏ", "các em" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 9:36: "em" is the warm, ordinary word for young children; Literal keeps the plain noun and pronoun.

decisions.choice: "손을 얹고 복을 빌어 주시기를"
decisions.reason: To touch here is to lay hands on them in blessing (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠγανάκτησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με, μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen now Jesus was indignant and said to them, Permit the little children to come to me, not do hinder them; for to such belongs the kingdom of God.

en.L: But when Jesus saw [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was indignant and said to them, "Permit the little children to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
en.B: When Jesus saw this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry and told them, "Allow the children to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Do not try to stop them, because it is to people like them that the kingdom of God belongs.
en.R: When Jesus saw what was happening, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said to them, "Let the children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! Do not keep them away. God's kingdom belongs to people who are like these children.

vi.L: Nhưng khi thấy [vậy], Đức Giê-xu bất bình và nói với họ: "Hãy để các trẻ nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đừng ngăn cản chúng, vì vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thuộc về những ai giống như chúng.
vi.B: Thấy vậy, Đức Giê-xu nổi giận và bảo họ: "Hãy để các em nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Đừng ngăn cản các em, vì vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thuộc về những người giống như các em.
vi.R: Khi thấy chuyện đang xảy ra, Đức Giê-xu nổi giận với các môn đồ. Ngài nói với họ: "Hãy để các em nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! Đừng ngăn các em lại. Vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thuộc về những người giống như các em này.

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 [그것을] 보시고 노하셔서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "어린아이들이 내게 오는 것을 허락하고, 그들을 막지 마라. 하나님의 나라는 이런 사람들의 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 이것을 보시고 노하셔서 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "어린아이들이 내게 오게 두어라. 막지 마라. 하나님의 나라는 이런 사람들의 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 이것을 보시고 제자들에게 화를 내셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "어린아이들이 내게 오게 해라! 막지 마라! 하나님의 나라는 이 아이들과 같은 사람들의 것이다.

decisions.choice: was indignant: became angry at a wrong
decisions.reason: The word is a strong one. It is used of the ten in 10:41 and of those who objected to the anointing (14:4). Only here is it used of Jesus.

decisions.choice: to such belongs the kingdom of God: to the children and to people like them
decisions.reason: "Such" includes the children and all who are like them. 10:15 explains how.

decisions.choice: the kingdom belongs to those with nothing to offer
decisions.reason: Children had no rank or claim. Mark does not praise their innocence; the kingdom is given to those who receive it as a gift.

decisions.choice: angry
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a common word for this strong feeling.

decisions.choice: with his followers
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Jesus was angry with.

decisions.choice: "bất bình" (L); "nổi giận" (B, R) for "was indignant"
decisions.reason: "bất bình" is anger at a wrong, close to the Greek; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời" for the kingdom of God, at every level
decisions.reason: As in John 3:3-5 and Mark 9; the same through Mark 10.

decisions.choice: "노하다" (L, B); "화를 내다" (R)
decisions.reason: He was angry at a wrong (meaning decision); "노하다" is the respectful word for anger with the honorific, as in Mark 3:5. "하나님의 나라" as in chapter 9, at every level.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, whoever not shall receive the kingdom of God as a child, no not shall enter into it.

en.L: Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will never enter into it."
en.B: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God the way a child does will never get into it."
en.R: I tell you the truth: you must welcome God's kingdom the way a child would. If you do not, you will never enter it."

vi.L: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ai không tiếp nhận vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời như một đứa trẻ thì nhất định sẽ không được vào đó."
vi.B: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ai không đón nhận vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời như một em nhỏ đón nhận thì chắc chắn sẽ không bao giờ được vào đó."
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con: các con phải đón nhận vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời như một em nhỏ. Nếu không, các con sẽ không bao giờ được vào đó."

ko.L: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 누구든지 하나님의 나라를 어린아이처럼 받아들이지 않으면, 결코 그곳에 들어가지 못할 것이다."
ko.B: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 누구든지 어린아이가 받아들이듯이 하나님의 나라를 받아들이지 않으면, 결코 그곳에 들어가지 못할 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 너희는 어린아이가 받아들이듯이 하나님의 나라를 받아들여야 한다. 그렇게 하지 않으면 결코 그 나라에 들어가지 못할 것이다."

decisions.choice: as a child: as a child receives it
alternatives: as one would receive a child
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean receiving the kingdom the way a child does, with trust and empty hands. They could also mean receiving the kingdom as one welcomes a child (9:37).

decisions.choice: never: a double negative, a strong denial
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make the warning firm.

decisions.choice: receive the kingdom and enter it: the kingdom is both a gift now and a place to enter
decisions.reason: The kingdom is received now and entered in the end, as in 9:47 and 10:23-25.

decisions.choice: you must welcome ... If you do not
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly and splits the warning into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các con" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các con" (R)
alternatives: "Quả thật, Ta nói với các con"
decisions.reason: Mark's single "Truly" takes one "Thật vậy", where John's double takes two; "các con" because Jesus is speaking to his disciples. The same in 10:29.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R), through chapter 10
decisions.reason: As in chapters 3 and 9: the single "amen" takes the Korean John's form, with a modern ending.

source.text: καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὰ κατευλόγει τιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken in arms them he was blessing, laying the hands on them.

en.L: And taking them in [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] arms, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was blessing [them], laying [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on them.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the children in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms, laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them, and blessed them.
en.R: Then Jesus took the children in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms. He put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on each of them and blessed them.

vi.L: Và ôm chúng vào lòng, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chúc phước [cho chúng], đặt tay trên chúng.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ôm các em vào lòng, đặt tay trên các em và chúc phước cho các em.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu ôm các em vào lòng. Ngài đặt tay trên từng em và chúc phước cho các em.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그들을 [팔에] 안으시고, 그들 위에 손을 얹으시며 축복하셨다.
ko.B: 그리고 예수께서는 아이들을 품에 안으시고, 그들에게 손을 얹으시며 복을 빌어 주셨다.
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서는 아이들을 품에 안아 주셨다. 아이들 하나하나에게 손을 얹으시고 복을 빌어 주셨다.

decisions.choice: was blessing: blessing warmly, a strengthened form of the verb
decisions.reason: Mark uses a strong form of the word for bless, found only here in the New Testament. Jesus gives more than the parents asked for.

decisions.choice: taking in arms: hugging, holding
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 9:36.

decisions.choice: was blessing: an imperfect, one child after another
decisions.reason: The tense pictures Jesus blessing them in turn.

decisions.choice: each of them
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the imperfect, blessing them one by one.

decisions.choice: "chúc phước" for "bless"
decisions.reason: "ban phước" is mostly said of God giving a blessing; Jesus here speaks a blessing over the children, which is "chúc phước".

decisions.choice: [팔에]
decisions.reason: As in 9:36: the Greek verb alone means to take in one's arms; Literal brackets the arms that Korean names. The hands need no bracket, since Korean says "손을 얹다" without a possessive.

source.text: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσδραμὼν εἷς καὶ γονυπετήσας αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσω ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;

records.literal_gloss: And going forth of him into [the] road, having run up one and having knelt to him was asking him, Teacher good, what shall I do that life eternal I might inherit?

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out onto the road, someone ran up and knelt before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and was asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Good Teacher, what must I do so that I may inherit eternal life?"
en.B: As Jesus was setting out on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} journey, a man ran up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, fell on his knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and asked, "Good Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?"
en.R: Jesus was starting on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way again. Then a man ran up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kneeled down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He asked, "Good Teacher, what do I have to do to receive eternal life from God?"

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ra đi lên đường, có một người chạy đến, quỳ trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy nhân lành, tôi phải làm gì để thừa hưởng sự sống đời đời?"
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu đang lên đường, có một người chạy đến, quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và hỏi: "Thưa Thầy nhân lành, tôi phải làm gì để được hưởng sự sống đời đời?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại lên đường. Lúc ấy có một người chạy đến và quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Người ấy hỏi: "Thưa Thầy tốt lành, tôi phải làm gì để nhận được sự sống đời đời từ Đức Chúa Trời?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 길을 나서실 때에, 한 사람이 달려와서 그분 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 그분께 물었다. "선한 선생님, 제가 영원한 생명을 상속받으려면 무엇을 해야 합니까?"
ko.B: 예수께서 길을 떠나실 때에, 어떤 사람이 달려와서 예수 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 여쭈었다. "선한 선생님, 제가 영원한 생명을 상속받으려면 무엇을 해야 합니까?"
ko.R: 예수께서 다시 길을 떠나시는데, 어떤 사람이 달려와서 예수 앞에 무릎을 꿇었다. 그리고 여쭈었다. "선한 선생님, 하나님께서 주시는 영원한 생명을 받으려면 제가 무엇을 해야 합니까?"

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: Eternal life is the life God gives in the coming age (Daniel 12:2). In 10:30 Jesus speaks of it as belonging to "the age to come", and here it stands beside entering the kingdom of God (10:23-25).

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as a share given by God
decisions.reason: Israel inherited the land as God's gift. The man asks what he must do to receive his share in the life to come.

decisions.choice: ran up and knelt: eagerness and deep respect
decisions.reason: A man of wealth (10:22) would not usually run in public. Kneeling shows great respect for Jesus.

decisions.choice: someone: Mark says only "one"
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who he was. Matthew 19:20 calls him a young man and Luke 18:18 a ruler. Mark tells only later that he was rich.

decisions.choice: a man
decisions.reason: The word "one" is masculine, and 10:20-22 shows it was a man. Readable adds "from God" to show where eternal life comes from.

decisions.choice: "Thưa Thầy nhân lành" (L, B), "Thưa Thầy tốt lành" (R); the man says "tôi", and Jesus calls him "anh" (10:18-21)
decisions.reason: "nhân lành" is goodness of character, the sense Jesus takes up in 10:18; Readable uses the plainer "tốt lành". The same word is kept in 10:18.

decisions.choice: "thừa hưởng" (L); "được hưởng" (B); "nhận được" (R) for "inherit"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of an inheritance; Balanced and Readable say it is received as God's gift.

decisions.choice: "영원한 생명" at every level; "상속받다" (L, B); "하나님께서 주시는 ... 받다" (R)
decisions.reason: "영원한 생명" is the term of the Korean John (style guide, section 6). To inherit is to receive a share given by God (meaning decision): Literal and Balanced keep "상속받다", and Readable says plainly who gives it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν;

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to him, Why me do you call good?

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?
en.B: Jesus answered, "Why are you calling {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?
en.R: Jesus answered, "Why do you say that I am good?

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với người ấy: "Sao anh gọi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là nhân lành?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Sao anh gọi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là nhân lành?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Tại sao anh nói {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là tốt lành?

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "어찌하여 너는 나를 선하다고 하느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "왜 너는 나를 선하다고 하느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "왜 너는 내가 선하다고 말하느냐?

decisions.choice: why do you call me good: Jesus makes the man think about what he has said
alternatives: Jesus denies that he is good
Jesus rebukes the man for flattery
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say he is not good. He turns the man's attention to God, the source of all goodness. A reader may see that the one who is good is speaking with God's authority.

decisions.choice: good: good in the full sense, as God is good
decisions.reason: Calling a teacher "good" was very rare. Jesus takes the word seriously.

decisions.choice: Why do you say that I am good
alternatives: Why do you call me good
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer way to say the same thing.

source.text: οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: No one good if not one, God.

en.L: No one [is] good except one, God.
en.B: No one is good except God alone.
en.R: Only God is good. No one else is.

vi.L: Không ai [là] nhân lành ngoại trừ một [Đấng], là Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Không ai nhân lành ngoại trừ một mình Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Chỉ có Đức Chúa Trời là tốt lành. Không có ai khác cả.

ko.L: 하나님 한 분 외에는 아무도 선하지 않다.
ko.B: 하나님 한 분 말고는 선한 이가 아무도 없다.
ko.R: 오직 하나님만 선하시다. 다른 누구도 선하지 않다.

decisions.choice: one, God: an echo of the Shema
decisions.reason: The words recall Deuteronomy 6:4, "the LORD is one", which Jesus quotes in 12:29. Only the one God is good in the full sense.

decisions.choice: except one, God: God alone
decisions.reason: The phrase means "except the one God" or "except God alone".

decisions.choice: Only God is good. No one else is.
alternatives: No one is good except God
decisions.reason: Readable states the positive first in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "하나님 한 분" (L, B); "오직 하나님만" (R)
decisions.reason: "One, God" echoes the Shema (meaning decision); Korean "한 분" keeps the word "one" with the honorific counter for God.

source.text: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.

records.literal_gloss: The commandments you know: Not you shall murder, not you shall commit adultery, not you shall steal, not you shall bear false witness, not you shall defraud, Honor the father of you and the mother.

en.L: You know the commandments: 'Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.'"
en.B: You know what the commandments say: 'Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not testify falsely. Do not cheat anyone. Honor your father and mother.'"
en.R: You know what God commands: 'Do not kill anyone. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about other people in court. Do not cheat anyone. Respect your father and mother.'"

vi.L: Anh biết các điều răn: 'Chớ giết người, chớ ngoại tình, chớ trộm cắp, chớ làm chứng dối, chớ lừa gạt, hãy hiếu kính cha mẹ anh.'"
vi.B: Anh biết các điều răn rồi: 'Đừng giết người. Đừng ngoại tình. Đừng trộm cắp. Đừng làm chứng dối. Đừng lừa gạt ai. Hãy hiếu kính cha mẹ.'"
vi.R: Anh biết những điều Đức Chúa Trời truyền dạy: 'Đừng giết người. Đừng ngoại tình. Đừng trộm cắp. Đừng nói dối để hại người khác trước tòa. Đừng lừa gạt ai. Hãy tôn trọng cha mẹ mình.'"

ko.L: 너는 계명들을 안다. '살인하지 마라, 간음하지 마라, 도둑질하지 마라, 거짓 증언하지 마라, 속여 빼앗지 마라, 네 아버지와 어머니를 공경하여라.'"
ko.B: 너는 계명을 알고 있다. '살인하지 마라. 간음하지 마라. 도둑질하지 마라. 거짓으로 증언하지 마라. 남의 것을 속여 빼앗지 마라. 네 아버지와 어머니를 공경하여라.'"
ko.R: 너는 하나님의 계명을 알고 있다. '사람을 죽이지 마라. 간음하지 마라. 도둑질하지 마라. 재판에서 남에 대해 거짓말하지 마라. 남을 속이지 마라. 네 아버지와 어머니를 존경하여라.'"

decisions.choice: the commandments: from the second half of the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: Jesus lists commandments about how to treat other people (Exodus 20:12-16; Deuteronomy 5:16-20), and puts honoring parents last.

decisions.choice: do not defraud: not one of the Ten, but drawn from the law
decisions.reason: The law forbids holding back a worker's wages (Deuteronomy 24:14; Leviticus 19:13; Malachi 3:5). Jesus may use it in place of "do not covet", or because it fits a rich man.

decisions.choice: do not defraud: in the SBLGNT text
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "do not defraud", perhaps because it is not one of the Ten Commandments or because Matthew and Luke lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: bear false witness: give false evidence against someone
decisions.reason: The commandment is about testimony in court, though it came to cover lying in general.

decisions.choice: kill anyone; tell lies about other people in court; respect
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words. "Murder" is the precise word; Readable adds "anyone" to make clear it means killing another person, not all killing.

decisions.choice: "Chớ" (L); "Đừng" (B, R) for the commandments' "Do not"
decisions.reason: "Chớ" has the weight of a law and is the familiar form for the commandments; "Đừng" is the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "계명"; modern imperatives "-지 마라", "-여라"
decisions.reason: "계명" is the word of the Korean John (13:34; 14:15). The commandments are quoted in modern spoken imperatives rather than the written "-지 말라" of familiar versions, since Jesus is speaking to the man.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα πάντα ἐφυλαξάμην ἐκ νεότητός μου.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to him, Teacher, these all I have kept from [the] youth of me.

en.L: And he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth."
en.B: "Teacher," he replied, "I have obeyed all of these since I was a boy."
en.R: The man said, "Teacher, I have obeyed all these laws ever since I was young."

vi.L: Và người ấy nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy, tôi đã giữ tất cả những điều này từ thuở nhỏ."
vi.B: Người ấy đáp: "Thưa Thầy, tôi đã vâng giữ tất cả những điều ấy từ khi còn nhỏ."
vi.R: Người ấy nói: "Thưa Thầy, tôi đã vâng giữ tất cả những luật ấy từ khi còn trẻ."

ko.L: 그러자 그가 그분께 말했다. "선생님, 저는 이 모든 것을 어려서부터 지켜 왔습니다."
ko.B: 그 사람이 대답했다. "선생님, 저는 어렸을 때부터 이 모든 것을 지켜 왔습니다."
ko.R: 그 사람이 말했다. "선생님, 저는 어릴 때부터 이 계명들을 다 지켜 왔습니다."

decisions.choice: youth: from boyhood, from the age a Jewish boy took on the law
decisions.reason: A Jewish boy became responsible for keeping the law around the age of thirteen.

decisions.choice: Teacher: this time without "good"
decisions.reason: The man drops the word "good" after Jesus' question in 10:18.

decisions.choice: I have kept all these: he believes he has obeyed them outwardly
decisions.reason: Jesus does not dispute his claim. Paul could say he was blameless as to the law's righteousness (Philippians 3:6).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ἠγάπησεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἕν σε ὑστερεῖ· ὕπαγε ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ δὸς τοῖς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus having looked at him loved him and said to him, One thing you is lacking; go, as much as you have sell and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven, and come follow me.

en.L: And Jesus, looking at him, loved him and said to him, "One thing you lack: go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Jesus looked at him and loved him. "You are missing one thing," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him. "Go and sell everything you own, and give the money to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: Jesus looked at the man and loved him. He said, "There is still one thing you need to do. Go and sell all you have. Give the money to poor people. Then you will have riches in heaven. And come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nhìn người ấy, yêu thương anh, và nói với anh: "Anh còn thiếu một điều: hãy đi, bán những gì anh có và cho người nghèo, thì anh sẽ có kho báu trên trời; rồi hãy đến, theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nhìn người ấy và yêu thương anh. Ngài bảo: "Anh còn thiếu một điều. Hãy đi bán hết những gì anh có và đem tiền cho người nghèo, rồi anh sẽ có kho báu trên trời. Sau đó, hãy đến và theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nhìn người ấy và yêu thương anh. Ngài nói: "Anh còn phải làm một điều nữa. Hãy đi bán hết những gì anh có, rồi đem tiền cho người nghèo. Như vậy anh sẽ có của cải trên trời. Rồi hãy đến và đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그를 바라보시고 그를 사랑하셔서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "네게 한 가지가 부족하다. 가서 네가 가진 것을 다 팔아 가난한 사람들에게 주어라. 그러면 네가 하늘에서 보물을 가지게 될 것이다. 그리고 와서 나를 따라라."
ko.B: 예수께서 그를 눈여겨보시고 사랑하셔서 말씀하셨다. "너에게 부족한 것이 하나 있다. 가서 네가 가진 것을 모두 팔아 그 돈을 가난한 사람들에게 주어라. 그러면 하늘에서 보물을 가지게 될 것이다. 그러고 나서 와서 나를 따라라."
ko.R: 예수께서 그 사람을 바라보시고 사랑하셨다. 그래서 말씀하셨다. "너에게 아직 해야 할 일이 하나 있다. 가서 네가 가진 것을 다 팔아라. 그 돈을 가난한 사람들에게 주어라. 그러면 하늘에 재물을 쌓게 될 것이다. 그리고 와서 나를 따라라."

decisions.choice: loved him: felt and showed love for him
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word for love. Mark alone says that Jesus loved him. His command comes from that love.

decisions.choice: looking at him: looking intently
decisions.reason: Mark uses this verb for a searching look (10:27; 14:67).

decisions.choice: treasure in heaven: riches kept by God
decisions.reason: Treasure in heaven is wealth that God keeps for a person and that cannot be lost (Matthew 6:20).

decisions.choice: the one thing lacking: to give up what holds him and follow Jesus
decisions.reason: The command to sell everything leads to the call "follow me". What he lacks is to follow Jesus with nothing held back.

decisions.choice: come, follow me: the SBLGNT ends here
alternatives: come, take up the cross, and follow me
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "take up the cross", most likely from 8:34. The earliest lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: There is still one thing you need to do; riches
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lack means, and uses a plain word for treasure.

decisions.choice: "yêu thương" for "loved"
decisions.reason: The verb John's Vietnamese renders "yêu"; "yêu thương" makes clear it is not romantic love.

source.text: ὁ δὲ στυγνάσας ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.

records.literal_gloss: And having been sad at the word he went away grieving; he was for having possessions many.

en.L: But his face fell at the word, and he went away grieving, for he was [one] who had many possessions.
en.B: At these words his face clouded over, and he went away sad, for he owned a great deal of property.
en.R: When the man heard this, he looked very unhappy. He went away sad, because he was very rich.

vi.L: Nhưng nghe lời ấy, người ấy sa sầm nét mặt và bỏ đi, buồn bã, vì anh là người có nhiều của cải.
vi.B: Nghe lời ấy, nét mặt anh sa sầm, và anh buồn bã bỏ đi, vì anh có rất nhiều tài sản.
vi.R: Khi nghe vậy, người ấy rất buồn. Anh buồn bã bỏ đi, vì anh rất giàu.

ko.L: 그러나 그는 그 말씀 때문에 얼굴빛이 어두워져서 근심하며 떠나갔다. 그는 재산이 많은 사람이었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 사람은 이 말씀을 듣고 얼굴이 어두워져서 슬퍼하며 떠나갔다. 그에게는 재산이 많았기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 이 말씀을 듣고 몹시 언짢은 얼굴이 되었다. 그리고 슬퍼하며 떠나갔다. 그는 큰 부자였기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: his face fell: he became gloomy, his face darkened
decisions.reason: The word is used of a dark, stormy sky in Matthew 16:3. His face showed his dismay.

decisions.choice: possessions: property, especially land and houses
decisions.reason: The word means what one owns, often fields and estates.

decisions.choice: for he was one who had: the reason he went away
alternatives: a later comment with no link
decisions.reason: Only now does Mark tell the reader the man was wealthy, and it explains his grief.

decisions.choice: he was very rich
decisions.reason: Readable says what having many possessions means.

source.text: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελεύσονται.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked around Jesus says to the disciples of him, How difficultly those the riches having into the kingdom of God will enter!

en.L: And looking around, Jesus says to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "How hard it will be for those who have riches to enter into the kingdom of God!"
en.B: Jesus looked around and told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!"
en.R: Jesus looked around at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said to them, "It is very hard for rich people to enter God's kingdom!"

vi.L: Và nhìn quanh, Đức Giê-xu nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Những người có của cải vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thật khó biết bao!"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nhìn quanh và nói với các môn đồ: "Người giàu có vào được vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thật khó biết bao!"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nhìn quanh các môn đồ. Ngài nói với họ: "Người giàu vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thật là khó!"

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 둘러보시고 그분의 제자들에게 말씀하신다. "재물을 가진 사람들이 하나님의 나라에 들어가기가 얼마나 어렵겠느냐!"
ko.B: 예수께서 둘러보시고 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "재물이 있는 사람들이 하나님의 나라에 들어가기는 참으로 어렵다!"
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들을 둘러보시며 말씀하셨다. "부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가기는 정말 어렵다!"

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: riches: money and wealth
decisions.reason: The word means money or property that can be used.

decisions.choice: how hard: wealth holds people back from the kingdom
alternatives: the rich are shut out by rule
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of difficulty here; 10:25-27 says it is impossible without God.

decisions.choice: looking around: as in 3:5 and 3:34, a look before a saying
decisions.reason: Mark uses the verb of Jesus looking around at those present before he speaks.

source.text: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the disciples were astonished at the words of him.

en.L: And the disciples were astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words.
en.B: The disciples were amazed at what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.
en.R: The followers were very surprised at what Jesus said.

vi.L: Và các môn đồ sững sờ trước những lời của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Các môn đồ kinh ngạc về những điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói.
vi.R: Các môn đồ rất ngạc nhiên về điều Đức Giê-xu nói.

ko.L: 그러자 제자들은 그분의 말씀에 놀랐다.
ko.B: 제자들은 예수의 말씀에 깜짝 놀랐다.
ko.R: 제자들은 예수의 말씀을 듣고 매우 놀랐다.

decisions.choice: were astonished: stunned, bewildered
decisions.reason: The word means a shocked surprise, as in 1:27. Many thought wealth was a sign of God's blessing (Deuteronomy 28:1-14), so Jesus' words overturned what they expected.

decisions.choice: were astonished: an imperfect, a lasting state
decisions.reason: The tense pictures their continuing bewilderment.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τέκνα, πῶς δύσκολόν ἐστιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν·

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus again answering says to them, Children, how difficult it is into the kingdom of God to enter!

en.L: But Jesus again responds and says to them, "Children, how hard it is to enter into the kingdom of God!
en.B: But Jesus said to them again, "My children, how hard it is to get into the kingdom of God!
en.R: But Jesus said again, "My children, it is very hard to enter God's kingdom!

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu lại đáp và nói với họ: "Hỡi các con, vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thật khó biết bao!
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ: "Này các con, vào được vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thật khó biết bao!
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu lại nói: "Các con ơi, vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thật là khó!

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 다시 대답하여 그들에게 말씀하신다. "자녀들아, 하나님의 나라에 들어가기가 얼마나 어려운지!
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서 다시 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "얘들아, 하나님의 나라에 들어가기는 참으로 어렵다!
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서 다시 말씀하셨다. "얘들아, 하나님의 나라에 들어가기는 정말 어렵다!

decisions.choice: children: a warm address to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to grown men as a teacher or father speaks to his own. Only here in Mark does he call his disciples "children".

decisions.choice: how hard it is to enter: in the SBLGNT, said of everyone
alternatives: how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "for those who trust in riches", which limits the saying to the rich. The earliest lack it, and the shorter text is harder: it is hard for anyone to enter. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: answering says: speaks again in response
decisions.reason: The disciples have not spoken; Jesus responds to their astonishment.

decisions.choice: My children
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "my" to keep the warmth of the address.

decisions.choice: "Hỡi các con" (L); "Này các con" (B); "Các con ơi" (R) for "Children"
decisions.reason: As John 21:5: "các con" is already how Jesus speaks to his disciples, and the address keeps its warmth at every level.

decisions.choice: "자녀들아" (L); "얘들아" (B, R)
decisions.reason: A warm address to the disciples (meaning decision); Literal keeps the word "children", and Balanced and Readable use the affectionate address the Korean John uses at 21:5.

source.text: εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς ῥαφίδος διελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Easier it is a camel through the eye of the needle to pass than a rich man into the kingdom of God to enter.

en.L: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of the needle than for {{gender:a rich person|a rich man}} to enter into the kingdom of God."
en.B: A camel could pass through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could enter the kingdom of God."
en.R: A camel is a very big animal, and the hole in a needle is very small. But a camel could get through that hole more easily than a rich person could enter God's kingdom."

vi.L: Con lạc đà đi qua lỗ kim còn dễ hơn người giàu vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Một con lạc đà chui qua lỗ kim còn dễ hơn một người giàu vào được vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Lạc đà là một con vật rất lớn, còn lỗ kim thì rất nhỏ. Thế nhưng một con lạc đà chui qua lỗ kim còn dễ hơn một người giàu vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."

ko.L: 낙타가 바늘귀로 지나가는 것이 부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것보다 더 쉽다."
ko.B: 부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것보다 낙타가 바늘귀로 지나가는 것이 더 쉽다."
ko.R: 낙타는 아주 큰 짐승이고, 바늘귀는 아주 작은 구멍이다. 그런데 부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것보다 낙타가 그 바늘귀로 빠져나가는 것이 더 쉽다."

decisions.choice: a camel through the eye of a needle: something impossible
alternatives: a small gate in Jerusalem called the needle
decisions.reason: The largest animal in the land and the smallest opening make a picture of what cannot happen. There is no early evidence for a gate called the needle's eye; that idea came much later. 10:27 shows that Jesus means it is impossible for people.

decisions.choice: camel
decisions.reason: A few late manuscripts read a similar Greek word meaning a ship's rope, which softens the picture. The SBLGNT and nearly all manuscripts read "camel". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a rich man: anyone who is rich
decisions.reason: The word is masculine in form but speaks of rich people in general.

decisions.choice: A camel is a very big animal, and the hole in a needle is very small
alternatives: a camel through the eye of the needle
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture so that young readers see the point.

decisions.choice: "người giàu" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese word already means any rich person, so the English gender span has no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "부자" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "부자" already means any rich person, man or woman, so the gender setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7).

source.text: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;

records.literal_gloss: And exceedingly they were astonished saying to themselves, And who is able to be saved?

en.L: And they were exceedingly astonished, saying to one another, "Then who can be saved?"
en.B: They were utterly amazed and said to each other, "Who can be saved, then?"
en.R: The followers were even more surprised. They said to each other, "Then who can be saved?"

vi.L: Và họ hết sức kinh ngạc, nói với nhau: "Vậy thì ai có thể được cứu?"
vi.B: Các môn đồ vô cùng kinh ngạc và nói với nhau: "Vậy thì ai có thể được cứu?"
vi.R: Các môn đồ lại càng ngạc nhiên hơn nữa. Họ nói với nhau: "Thế thì ai có thể được cứu?"

ko.L: 그러자 그들은 더욱 몹시 놀라서 서로 말했다. "그러면 누가 구원받을 수 있는가?"
ko.B: 제자들은 더욱 크게 놀라서 서로 말했다. "그렇다면 누가 구원받을 수 있겠는가?"
ko.R: 제자들은 더욱더 놀랐다. 그래서 서로 말했다. "그러면 누가 구원받을 수 있겠느냐?"

decisions.choice: be saved: be rescued by God and given life in his kingdom
decisions.reason: Here being saved means the same as entering the kingdom and inheriting eternal life (10:17, 23).

decisions.choice: then: if even the rich cannot, who can
decisions.reason: The word draws a conclusion from what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: saying to one another
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "saying to him", so that the disciples ask Jesus. The SBLGNT reads "to themselves", that is, to one another. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: The followers were even more surprised
decisions.reason: Readable names who was amazed and links this to 10:24.

decisions.choice: "구원받다"
decisions.reason: To be saved is to be rescued by God and given life in his kingdom (meaning decision); "구원" is the word of the Korean John (10:9; 12:47). The disciples speak among themselves in the plain style.

source.text: ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον ἀλλ’ οὐ παρὰ θεῷ, πάντα γὰρ δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Having looked at them Jesus says, With men impossible, but not with God; all things for possible with God.

en.L: Looking at them, Jesus says, "With {{gender:people|men}} [it is] impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God."
en.B: Jesus looked straight at them and said, "For human beings it cannot be done, but not for God. God can do anything."
en.R: Jesus looked at them and said, "People cannot do this. But God can. God can do everything."

vi.L: Nhìn họ, Đức Giê-xu nói: "Đối với loài người, [điều đó là] không thể, nhưng đối với Đức Chúa Trời thì không; vì đối với Đức Chúa Trời mọi sự đều có thể."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nhìn thẳng vào họ và nói: "Đối với loài người thì không thể được, nhưng đối với Đức Chúa Trời thì không phải vậy. Đức Chúa Trời làm được mọi sự."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nhìn họ và nói: "Con người không thể làm được điều này. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời thì làm được. Đức Chúa Trời làm được mọi việc."

ko.L: 예수께서 그들을 바라보시며 말씀하신다. "사람에게는 불가능하지만 하나님께는 그렇지 않다. 하나님께는 모든 것이 가능하기 때문이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들을 똑바로 바라보시며 말씀하셨다. "사람은 할 수 없지만, 하나님은 그렇지 않으시다. 하나님께서는 무엇이든 하실 수 있다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들을 바라보시며 말씀하셨다. "사람은 이 일을 할 수 없다. 그러나 하나님은 하실 수 있다. 하나님께서는 모든 것을 하실 수 있다."

decisions.choice: all things are possible with God: the faith of Israel's Scriptures
decisions.reason: The words recall Genesis 18:14, "Is anything too hard for the LORD?", said when Sarah was promised a son, and Job 42:2.

decisions.choice: impossible with people, not with God: salvation is God's work
alternatives: the rich can save themselves with effort
decisions.reason: No one, rich or poor, can enter by human power. God alone can bring them in.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: God can do anything (B); God can do everything (R)
alternatives: all things are possible with God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the same thing with God as the subject.

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L, B), "con người" (R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words already mean human beings.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "사람" already includes men and women; the English span has nothing to match in Korean (style guide, section 7).

source.text: Ἤρξατο λέγειν ὁ Πέτρος αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήκαμέν σοι.

records.literal_gloss: Began to say Peter to him, Behold, we have left all and have followed you.

en.L: Peter began to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, we have left everything and have followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Peter spoke up: "Look, we have left everything behind to follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Then Peter said to Jesus, "Look at us! We have left everything we had, and we have followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

vi.L: Phi-e-rơ bắt đầu nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Này, chúng con đã bỏ mọi sự và đã đi theo Thầy."
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ lên tiếng thưa: "Thầy xem, chúng con đã bỏ hết mọi sự để theo Thầy."
vi.R: Rồi Phi-e-rơ thưa với Đức Giê-xu: "Thầy nhìn chúng con đây! Chúng con đã bỏ hết mọi thứ mình có, và chúng con đã đi theo Thầy."

ko.L: 베드로가 그분께 말하기 시작했다. "보십시오, 우리는 모든 것을 버리고 선생님을 따랐습니다."
ko.B: 베드로가 나서서 말했다. "보십시오, 저희는 모든 것을 버리고 선생님을 따랐습니다."
ko.R: 그러자 베드로가 예수께 말했다. "저희를 보십시오! 저희는 가진 것을 다 버리고 선생님을 따라왔습니다."

decisions.choice: have left, have followed: perfects, a step taken that still holds
decisions.reason: The tense shows a decision made in the past that continues. Peter contrasts the disciples with the rich man.

decisions.choice: look: calls attention to what follows
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what Peter is about to say.

decisions.choice: we have left everything: as Peter and Andrew left their nets (1:18)
decisions.reason: James and John left their father in the boat (1:20) and Levi left his tax booth (2:14).

decisions.choice: "chúng con" and "Thầy" in the disciples' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark 9: the disciples speak to Jesus as their teacher; the same in 10:35-39.

source.text: ἔφη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ μητέρα ἢ πατέρα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ἐὰν μὴ λάβῃ ἑκατονταπλασίονα νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ μητέρας καὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀγροὺς μετὰ διωγμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: Was saying Jesus, Truly I say to you, no one there is who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or lands for the sake of me and for the sake of the gospel, \v 30 if not he shall receive a hundredfold now in the time this, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and lands, with persecutions, and in the age the coming life eternal.

en.L: Jesus said, "Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake and for the sake of the gospel \v 30 who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life.
en.B: Jesus said, "Truly I tell you, anyone who has left a home, brothers or sisters, mother or father, children or land because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and because of the gospel \v 30 will receive a hundred times as much now, in this present time: homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and land, together with persecutions. And in the age that is coming they will receive eternal life.
en.R: Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: some people have left their homes, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children or farms because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and the good news. \v 30 Every one of them will get a hundred times as much in this life. They will have homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and farms. People will also treat them cruelly for following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And in the world to come they will have eternal life.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, không có ai đã bỏ nhà cửa, hoặc anh em, hoặc chị em, hoặc mẹ, hoặc cha, hoặc con cái, hoặc ruộng đất vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì Tin Lành, \v 30 mà không nhận được gấp trăm lần ngay bây giờ trong đời này: nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, con cái và ruộng đất, cùng với sự bắt bớ, và trong đời sắp đến thì [nhận được] sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ai đã bỏ nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, cha, con cái hay ruộng đất vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì Tin Lành, \v 30 thì ngay trong đời này sẽ nhận được gấp trăm lần: nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, con cái và ruộng đất, cùng với sự bắt bớ. Và trong đời sắp đến, người ấy sẽ nhận được sự sống đời đời.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ta nói thật với các con: có những người đã bỏ nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, cha, con cái hay ruộng vườn vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì Tin Lành. \v 30 Mỗi người trong họ sẽ nhận lại gấp trăm lần ngay trong đời này. Họ sẽ có nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, con cái và ruộng vườn. Người ta cũng sẽ bắt bớ họ vì họ theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và trong đời sắp đến, họ sẽ có sự sống đời đời.

ko.L: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나 때문에, 그리고 복음 때문에 집이나 형제나 자매나 어머니나 아버지나 자녀나 밭을 버린 사람은, \v 30 지금 이 시대에 집과 형제와 자매와 어머니와 자녀와 밭을 박해와 함께 백 배나 받고, 오는 세상에서는 영원한 생명을 받지 않는 사람이 없다.
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나 때문에, 그리고 복음 때문에 집이나 형제나 자매나 어머니나 아버지나 자녀나 밭을 버린 사람은, \v 30 지금 이 세상에서 집과 형제와 자매와 어머니와 자녀와 밭을 백 배나 받을 것이다. 박해도 함께 받을 것이다. 그리고 오는 세상에서는 영원한 생명을 받을 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "내가 분명히 말한다. 나 때문에, 그리고 기쁜 소식 때문에 자기 집이나 형제나 자매나 어머니나 아버지나 자녀나 농토를 떠난 사람들이 있다. \v 30 그런 사람은 누구나 이 세상에서 백 배나 받을 것이다. 집과 형제와 자매와 어머니와 자녀와 농토를 얻게 될 것이다. 또 나를 따른다는 이유로 사람들에게 괴롭힘도 당할 것이다. 그리고 앞으로 올 세상에서는 영원한 생명을 얻을 것이다.

decisions.choice: a hundredfold now: a new family and shared homes among Jesus' followers
alternatives: great personal wealth in this life
decisions.reason: Jesus has already called those who do God's will his brother and sister and mother (3:34-35). Those who leave family find a far larger family among his followers, who share their homes.

decisions.choice: mothers, but not fathers: the second list leaves out fathers
decisions.reason: The new family has mothers, but Jesus does not name fathers. It may be because God alone is Father in this family (11:25; Matthew 23:9). Mark does not explain.

decisions.choice: persecutions: harassment and suffering for following Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus does not promise ease. The gift of the new family comes with suffering, as in 4:17 and 13:9-13.

decisions.choice: the age to come, eternal life: the life of God's coming age
decisions.reason: Jews spoke of this age and the age to come. Eternal life belongs to the age to come, and it answers the man's question in 10:17.

decisions.choice: mother or father: the SBLGNT list has no wife
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "or wife" to the first list, as in Luke 18:29. The earliest lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: no one who ... who will not receive: everyone who has left will receive
decisions.reason: The double negative makes a firm promise to all who have left these things.

decisions.choice: anyone who has left ... will receive (B); some people have left ... Every one of them will get (R)
alternatives: there is no one who has left ... who will not receive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the double negative into a positive promise. Readable splits the long sentence and says what persecutions are.

decisions.choice: "Tin Lành" for the gospel, at every level
decisions.reason: As in Colossians. The Protestant word already means "good news", so Readable needs no other word where the English Readable says "good news".

decisions.choice: "đời sắp đến" for "the age to come"
decisions.reason: "đời sau" would suggest only life after death; "đời sắp đến" keeps the coming age of God, set against "đời này" (this time).

decisions.choice: "복음" (L, B); "기쁜 소식" (R)
decisions.reason: Key term: "gospel" at Literal and Balanced, "good news" at Readable, as the English does and as the Korean Colossians does (1:23).

decisions.choice: the double negative "no one ... who will not receive" is kept at the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: Korean can keep the Greek's "there is no one who ... does not receive" only by putting "없다" last; Balanced and Readable say it positively, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "박해" (L, B); "괴롭힘을 당하다" (R)
decisions.reason: "박해" is the word of the Korean John (15:20); "핍박" is the older church word. Readable uses the everyday word.

source.text: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.

records.literal_gloss: Many however will be first last and the last first.

en.L: But many [who are] first will be last, and the last first."
en.B: Yet many who are first will end up last, and the last first."
en.R: But many people who are important now will be the least important then. And many who are the least important now will be the most important."

vi.L: Nhưng nhiều người đứng đầu sẽ thành người cuối cùng, và những người cuối cùng [sẽ thành] người đứng đầu."
vi.B: Nhưng nhiều người đang đứng đầu sẽ trở thành người cuối cùng, và những người cuối cùng sẽ được đứng đầu."
vi.R: Nhưng nhiều người bây giờ đang quan trọng thì khi ấy sẽ trở thành kém quan trọng nhất. Và nhiều người bây giờ kém quan trọng nhất thì khi ấy sẽ trở thành quan trọng nhất."

ko.L: 그러나 첫째인 많은 사람이 꼴찌가 되고, 꼴찌인 [많은 사람이] 첫째가 될 것이다."
ko.B: 그러나 첫째인 많은 사람이 꼴찌가 되고, 꼴찌인 많은 사람이 첫째가 될 것이다."
ko.R: 그러나 지금 높은 사람들 가운데 많은 사람이 그때에는 가장 낮아질 것이다. 그리고 지금 가장 낮은 사람들 가운데 많은 사람이 그때에는 가장 높아질 것이다."

decisions.choice: first and last: God reverses human ranking
alternatives: a rule about lines or order
decisions.reason: Those honored now, like the rich, may be last in the kingdom, and those who gave up everything may be first. The saying may also warn the disciples not to count on their own place.

decisions.choice: first last: the first will be last
decisions.reason: The verb "will be" links each pair: the first become last, the last become first.

decisions.choice: important now ... least important then
decisions.reason: Readable says what first and last mean and when the change comes.

decisions.choice: [많은 사람이]
decisions.reason: The Greek says "many" once for both halves; Korean repeats it in the second half, so Literal brackets the repetition.

source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ἦν προάγων αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο, οἱ δὲ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο.

records.literal_gloss: They were then on the road going up to Jerusalem, and was going on before them Jesus, and they were astonished, and those following were afraid.

en.L: And they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were astonished, and those who followed were afraid.
en.B: They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, with Jesus going on ahead of them. The disciples were astonished, and the others who followed were afraid.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were on the road going up to Jerusalem. Jesus was walking out in front of them. The disciples were amazed at this. The others who were following were afraid.

vi.L: Bấy giờ họ đang trên đường đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, và Đức Giê-xu đi trước họ; họ kinh ngạc, còn những người đi theo thì sợ hãi.
vi.B: Họ đang trên đường đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, và Đức Giê-xu đi trước họ. Các môn đồ kinh ngạc, còn những người khác đi theo thì sợ hãi.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ đang trên đường đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Đức Giê-xu đi phía trước họ. Các môn đồ rất ngạc nhiên về điều đó. Những người khác đi theo thì sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그들은 예루살렘으로 올라가는 길에 있었다. 그리고 예수께서 그들보다 앞서 가고 계셨다. 그러자 그들은 놀랐고, 따라오는 사람들은 두려워했다.
ko.B: 그들은 예루살렘으로 올라가는 길에 있었다. 예수께서는 그들보다 앞장서서 가고 계셨다. 제자들은 놀랐고, 뒤따르는 다른 사람들은 두려워했다.
ko.R: 예수와 제자들은 예루살렘으로 올라가는 길에 있었다. 예수께서는 그들 앞에서 앞장서 걸어가셨다. 제자들은 그것을 보고 놀랐다. 뒤따라오던 다른 사람들은 두려워했다.

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: Jerusalem stands high in the hills
decisions.reason: Travelers always went up to Jerusalem, which lies high in the hills of Judea. Pilgrims coming to the Passover took the road from Jericho (10:46).

decisions.choice: they were astonished, those who followed were afraid: perhaps two groups
alternatives: one group, the disciples, both amazed and afraid
decisions.reason: Mark may mean the disciples were amazed while others in the crowd following were afraid. He may also be describing the same people in two ways.

decisions.choice: Jesus was going ahead of them: he leads the way to his suffering
alternatives: he was walking alone by chance
decisions.reason: Jesus walks in front, knowing what waits in Jerusalem (8:31; 9:31). His resolve amazes and frightens those behind him.

decisions.choice: The disciples ... the others who followed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two groups as Mark seems to mean them. This follows the more likely reading.

source.text: καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν, καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken again the twelve he began them to tell the things being about him to happen, \v 33 Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and to the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and will hand over him to the Gentiles, \v 34 and they will mock him and will spit upon him and will flog him and will kill, and after three days he will rise.

en.L: And taking the twelve aside again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to tell them the things that were about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: \v 33 "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death and will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles, \v 34 and they will mock {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and flog {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kill [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], and after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."
